# Results — Study 918 (Creation Halt) on the real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Six hardcoded, publicly
reported suspensions of share issuance (or, for GBTC, of redemption). For each we build
the **signed tracking spread** — the daily log-return difference between the capped fund
and an **uncapped** instrument tracking the same thing, signed `+1` for a creation
suspension and `−1` for a redemption suspension — and run an event study on it. Daily
**total-return** closes (`yfinance`, `auto_adjust=True`) for every ETF/ETN leg; `NG=F` is
a **price-only** continuous front-month futures print. One execution lag throughout: a
suspension announced on day `t` is acted on at the close of `t+1`, so every window starts
at `t+1` and the announcement-day move is excluded. As-of **2026-06-30**.*

## Data stamp

| Legs | Window | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|
| UNG, USO, VXX, OIL, GBTC, BITO + NG=F, DBO, BNO, USL, VIXY, BTC-USD, BIL | 1990-01-02 → 2026-06-30 (per-leg listing dates below) | `696cca301c40` |

| Event | Pair | Dir | Ruler | Confidence | Spread window | sd |
|---|---|--:|---|---|---|--:|
| UNG-2009 | UNG vs NG=F | +1 | curve-mismatched | APPROX | 2007-04-19 → 2026-06-30 | 2.05%/d |
| USO-2020 | USO vs DBO | +1 | curve-mismatched | APPROX | 2007-01-08 → 2026-06-30 | 0.92%/d |
| VXX-2022 | VXX vs VIXY | +1 | **exact** | FIRM | 2018-01-26 → 2026-06-30 | 0.85%/d |
| OIL-2022 | OIL vs DBO | +1 | curve-mismatched | FIRM | 2011-04-21 → 2023-07-21 | 1.17%/d |
| GBTC-2024 | GBTC vs BTC-USD | −1 | **exact** | resume FIRM, start = tape start | 2015-05-12 → 2026-06-30 | 3.44%/d |
| BITO-2021 | BITO vs BTC-USD | +1 | curve-mismatched | SOFT | 2021-10-21 → 2026-06-30 | 1.48%/d |

**Excess-of-cash.** The spread is one dollar long the fund funded by one dollar short the
twin, so the cash leg cancels: `(r_f − r_c) − (r_p − r_c) ≡ r_f − r_p`. The check printed
by `verify.py` returns `0.00e+00` for all six pairs against BIL, but that is an
**algebraic identity, not a finding** — it cannot come out otherwise, and it is run only
to prove the code path never races a raw return against an excess return. The economic
claim behind it (that a short rebate is the full cash rate) is *false* for a
hard-to-borrow name, which is why the short leg is charged borrow explicitly and swept
from 0 to 30 %/yr in §5.

**Three mechanical contaminants, named up front.** (1) The spread carries the two legs'
**expense-ratio difference** before any halt effect exists — column `fee` in §2; it is
material only for GBTC (+0.79 bps/day against an unfeed spot ruler, 18% of its measured
drift). (2) The `hold = halt` trade in §5a **exits on the resumption date, which nobody
knew at entry** — §5b is the no-look-ahead version. (3) The placebo pools below step one
session at a time, so their windows overlap by `(k−1)/k`; **`pct_indep` is the same
percentile on non-overlapping windows** and is the one to read.

## Multiplicity

Five announcement events × three horizons (K = 5/10/20) × two legs (announcement, fade)
= **30 placebo percentiles are looked at** before any winner is quoted. The family-wise
5% bar for a single one-sided look is therefore percentile **≥ 0.99833**. This matters:
the study's best single number sits just under it.

## 1. The announcement event study

K-day cumulative signed spread starting the session *after* the suspension is announced,
standardised against that pair's own distribution of K-day windows away from the event.
`pct` uses overlapping windows; **`pct_indep` uses non-overlapping ones and is the honest
denominator.** GBTC has no announcement day — its suspension was a standing regime from
the first listed session — so it appears only from §2 onward.

| Event | K = 5 CAR (z) | K = 10 CAR (z) | K = 20 CAR (z) | pct (K=20) | **pct_indep** (n) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| UNG-2009 | +2.99% (+0.97) | +1.36% (+0.55) | −3.30% (−0.24) | 0.278 | 0.277 (235) |
| USO-2020 | **−25.61% (−13.55)** | −13.58% (−5.53) | −6.00% (−1.63) | 0.027 | 0.025 (241) |
| VXX-2022 | +11.42% (+8.96) | +19.10% (+14.33) | **+15.41% (+13.84)** | 0.999 | **0.990 (99)** |
| OIL-2022 | +1.69% (+0.95) | +2.31% (+0.99) | −7.03% (−2.55) | 0.014 | 0.014 (148) |
| BITO-2021 | −2.83% (−1.87) | −0.72% (−0.36) | −0.95% (−0.36) | 0.325 | 0.352 (54) |
| **pooled** | mean z **−0.91**, *t* = −0.25, 3/5 positive | mean z **+2.00**, *t* = +0.61, 3/5 positive | mean z **+1.81**, *t* = +0.60, **1/5 positive** | | event-resample CI [−1.90, +7.93] |

The pooled cross-event *t* never clears 1 at any horizon, and the sign of the pooled mean
flips with the horizon. One event carries everything.

**On `z`.** These spreads are strongly mean-reverting and fat-tailed, so a k-day sum is
nowhere near Gaussian and `z` is a scale, not a p-value: VXX's `z = +13.84` sits at
empirical percentile 0.990, not at the 1e−43 a normal table would give. Read the
percentile. And read `pct_indep`: VXX's 8.5-year tape contains **99** independent 20-day
windows, not 1,978, so the strongest honest claim is one-sided *p* ≈ 0.010 — which does
**not** clear the 30-look bar of 0.99833 on its own.

## 2. Drift while issuance is suspended

Mean daily signed spread from the session after the announcement through the resumption
date, versus every other session for the same pair **excluding the 20 sessions after
resumption**. That exclusion cuts against the hypothesis and is the point: leaving the
fade window in the control depresses the baseline and flatters the gap (on VXX it moved
the control from −0.49 to +0.43 bps/day). `fee` is the expense-ratio difference already
baked into the spread — an ASSUMPTION from published prospectus figures, not tape.

| Event | in-halt days | in-halt bps/d (HAC *t*) | total | `fee` | net-of-fee | out bps/d (*t*, n) | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| UNG-2009 | 58 | −20.12 (−0.60) | −11.01% | −0.54 | −19.58 | −10.72 (−5.33, 4750) | −0.23 |
| USO-2020 | 6 | −351.48 (−2.09) | −19.01% | −0.01 | −351.48 | −2.27 (−1.73, 4874) | −1.00 |
| VXX-2022 | 101 | **+17.72 (+0.71)** | **+19.59%** | −0.02 | +17.73 | +0.43 (+0.67, 1996) | +0.68 |
| OIL-2022 | 101 | −2.11 (−0.25) | −2.11% | +0.01 | −2.12 | +0.66 (+0.49, 2961) | −0.32 |
| GBTC-2024 | 2,183 | **+4.35 (+0.67)** | **+158.56%** | **+0.79** | **+3.56** | +0.77 (+0.34, 597) | +0.36 |
| BITO-2021 | 43 | −9.09 (−0.67) | −3.83% | −0.38 | −8.71 | −1.99 (−1.24, 1113) | −0.30 |

The two events whose ruler is **exact** (VXX vs VIXY, GBTC vs spot bitcoin) are the only
two that drift the predicted way. Both HAC *t*s are below 1 and every Welch *t* on the
difference is below 1 in absolute value: the divergence arrives in lumps, not as a steady
daily accrual. **Eighteen percent of GBTC's drift is simply its 2%/yr management fee**
measured against an unfeed spot price, and GBTC has no pre-halt control at all — its 597
"outside" sessions are entirely post-conversion.

## 3. The fade when issuance resumes (K = 20, window starts resume+1)

| Event | CAR | z | pct | **pct_indep** (n) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| UNG-2009 | **−28.29%** | **−5.02** | 0.002 | 0.000 (235) |
| USO-2020 | +14.58% | +4.25 | 0.999 | 1.000 (241) |
| VXX-2022 | **−18.48%** | **−16.83** | 0.000 | **0.000 (99)** |
| OIL-2022 | +0.16% | +0.00 | 0.540 | 0.514 (148) |
| GBTC-2024 | −2.64% | −0.31 | 0.267 | 0.259 (135) |
| BITO-2021 | +0.24% | +0.42 | 0.710 | 0.704 (54) |
| **pooled** | | mean z **−2.91**, cross-event *t* = **−0.96** | 3/6 negative | CI [−9.11, +1.49] |

The fade is the folklore's most convincing leg: the two funds that verifiably *had* a
premium (UNG in 2009, VXX in 2022) both gave it back violently within a month of
issuance restarting, and both are the single most extreme window in their own
non-overlapping history. It is still not a pooled result — USO went the other way by
+14.6%, at the opposite extreme.

## 4. Robustness

**Jackknife (K = 20, leave one announcement event out).** Everything is VXX:

| Dropped | mean z | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| UNG-2009 | +2.33 | +0.60 |
| USO-2020 | +2.67 | +0.71 |
| **VXX-2022** | **−1.19** | **−2.17** |
| OIL-2022 | +2.90 | +0.79 |
| BITO-2021 | +2.35 | +0.61 |

**Ruler-quality split (K = 20).** The informative cut:

| Ruler | n | mean z | *t* | positive |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| exact (tracks the very thing the fund holds) | 1 | +13.84 | n/a | 1/1 |
| curve-mismatched (a different point on a futures curve) | 4 | −1.19 | −2.17 | 0/4 |

**Calendar era cut (split 2020-01-01).** Uninformative by construction — 1 event before,
4 after (early mean z −0.24; late mean z +2.33, *t* = +0.60). The hardcoded event list is
too small and too clustered for a calendar cut to say anything.

**Resumption-date sweep** (the APPROX/SOFT dates shifted ±10 business days; the FIRM
dates are left alone):

| Shift | mean fade z | mean in-halt bps/d | fades negative |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| −10 bd | −5.94 | −0.36 | 5/6 |
| −5 bd | −3.38 | −235.57 | 4/6 |
| 0 bd | −2.91 | −60.12 | 3/6 |
| +5 bd | −2.80 | −26.98 | 3/6 |
| +10 bd | −3.03 | −19.89 | 4/6 |

The fade direction survives the sweep; the in-halt drift number does not (USO's window is
six sessions long, so a five-day shift moves it by hundreds of bps/day). Anything that
depends on the exact resumption date is not a result.

## 5. Tradability — long the capped fund, short the uncapped twin

Costs: 10 bps one-way × NAV on **both** legs at entry and exit (four crossings); a
**daily rebalancing charge** of `10 bps × Σ|xₜ|`, because `exp(Σx)` is the return of a
position held at constant dollar neutrality and holding one flat costs turnover; and
**3%/yr borrow** on the short leg per calendar day held.

### 5a. Hindsight exit — held to the resumption date, which nobody knew at entry

| Event | days | gross | cost | rebal | borrow | **net** |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| UNG-2009 | 58 | −11.01% | 0.40% | 0.13% | 0.68% | **−12.22%** |
| USO-2020 | 6 | −19.01% | 0.40% | 0.04% | 0.07% | **−19.52%** |
| VXX-2022 | 101 | +19.59% | 0.40% | 0.19% | 1.21% | **+17.80%** |
| OIL-2022 | 101 | −2.11% | 0.40% | 0.06% | 1.21% | **−3.78%** |
| GBTC-2024 | 2,183 | +158.56% | 0.40% | **5.73%** | 26.03% | **+126.40%** |
| BITO-2021 | 43 | −3.83% | 0.40% | 0.05% | 0.52% | **−4.80%** |

Mean net **+17.31%**, **median net −4.29%**, 2/6 positive, cross-event *t* = **+0.77**.
The mean is positive only because GBTC's 8.7-year discount build is counted as one
"trade": **ex-GBTC the mean net is −4.51% with 1/5 positive**.

### 5b. Blind exit — the rule you could actually have followed

Enter at `t+1`, exit after a **fixed 60 sessions**, with no knowledge of when issuance
would resume. This is the honest tradability number, and it is the audit's most damaging
result:

| Event | days | gross | rebal | borrow | **net** |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| UNG-2009 | 60 | −31.73% | 0.16% | 0.70% | **−32.98%** |
| USO-2020 | 60 | −5.26% | 0.08% | 0.71% | **−6.45%** |
| VXX-2022 | 60 | +1.81% | 0.13% | 0.71% | **+0.57%** |
| OIL-2022 | 60 | −0.99% | 0.04% | 0.71% | **−2.14%** |
| GBTC-2024 | 60 | +97.90% | 0.17% | 0.71% | **+96.62%** |
| BITO-2021 | 60 | −7.29% | 0.08% | 0.72% | **−8.49%** |

Mean **+7.86%**, median **−4.29%**, 2/6 positive, cross-event *t* = **+0.43**.
**VXX — the flagship event, the one clean ruler, the +15.4% CAR — nets +0.57% once you
stop being told when the halt ends.** Its entire tradable profit was the hindsight exit.
(GBTC's +96.62% is not a halt trade at all: it is 60 arbitrary days inside an 8.7-year
regime, and its window is the same 60 sessions whichever rule you use.)

**Cost × borrow sweep** (mean / median per-event net, hindsight exit):

| borrow | 0 bps cost | 5 bps | 10 bps | 25 bps |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0%/yr | +23.70 / −2.97 | +22.98 / −3.20 | +22.26 / −3.43 | +20.12 / −4.11 |
| 3%/yr | +18.75 / −3.84 | +18.03 / −4.06 | +17.31 / −4.29 | +15.16 / −4.97 |
| 10%/yr | +7.19 / −5.85 | +6.47 / −6.08 | +5.76 / −6.30 | +3.61 / −6.99 |
| 30%/yr | −25.82 / −16.02 | −26.54 / −16.26 | −27.26 / −16.51 | −29.40 / −17.25 |

Commissions are near-irrelevant on the short holds; **borrow is decisive**. At the 30%/yr
a hard-to-borrow capped ETP actually costs, the mean net is −27% and only 1/6 events pays.
The borrow rate is an **ASSUMPTION** — no free source publishes historical ETP borrow —
which is exactly why it is swept rather than picked.

## 6. The one clean suspension, close up (VXX vs VIXY, 2022-03-14 → 2022-08-08)

Two instruments tracking the *same* short-dated VIX-futures index; one capped for five
months, one not.

- Announcement-day move **+5.81%** — **excluded** by the execution lag, so none of it is
  claimed.
- In-halt: 101 sessions, **+17.72 bps/d**, total **+19.59%**, spread Sharpe +1.10, but
  **HAC *t* = +0.71** and a block-bootstrap CI on the daily mean of **[−30.3, +69.1]
  bps/d** with 25.3% of resamples negative. The level move is unmistakable; the *daily
  drift* is not statistically separable from zero.
- **The premium round-trips inside the halt.** It is not a monotone accretion, and this
  is why the blind trade earns nothing:

  | K | 5 | 10 | 20 | 40 | 60 | 101 |
  |---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
  | CAR | +11.42% | +19.10% | +15.41% | **−1.06%** | +1.79% | +17.89% |

- Announcement CAR at K = 20 is percentile **0.990** and the fade percentile **0.000**,
  of only **99 independent** 20-day windows. Against the 30-look family-wise bar of
  0.99833, **neither tail clears on its own**. What does clear is the *joint* pattern —
  both tails, in the two directions the mechanism predicts, on the two dates it names,
  in the one pair with an exact ruler (joint one-sided *p* ≈ 1e−4 before multiplicity,
  ≈ 1.5e−3 against the 15 joint looks in the design). That joint pattern is the entire
  positive evidence in this study, and it is n = 1.

## 7. Synthetic control (machinery proof — never supports the stamp)

Six planted pairs per draw, 8 seeds each:

| World | pooled announcement *t* | \|*t*\| ≥ 2 | in-halt drift | fade z |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| planted (12 bps/d) | +2.56 | 5/8 | +10.42 bps/d | −4.73 |
| half strength (6 bps/d) | +0.94 | 3/8 | +4.88 bps/d | −2.37 |
| **null (nothing planted)** | **−0.73** | **1/8** | **−0.66 bps/d** | **+0.02** |

The estimator recovers a planted halt premium, degrades gracefully at half strength, and
is silent on the null. It also shows how little power six events buy: even a *real*
12 bps/day premium clears |*t*| ≥ 2 in only five draws out of eight.

## Verdict

- **Signal — Mixed.** The mechanism is visible where it can be measured and absent
  everywhere else. In the one suspension with an **exact** ruler — VXX capped while VIXY,
  holding the same index, was not — the fund repriced **+15.4%** in the 20 lagged sessions
  after the announcement and handed back **−18.5%** in the 20 sessions after issuance
  resumed. Stated honestly, that is percentile **0.990 and 0.000 of 99 independent**
  20-day windows: *neither tail clears the 30-look family-wise bar alone*, and it is the
  **joint** announce-and-fade pattern, on the two dates the mechanism names, that survives
  multiplicity. The other exact-ruler case (GBTC) drifts the predicted way but at
  HAC *t* = +0.67, with 18% of the drift being nothing but its 2%/yr fee. And it does
  **not** generalise: pooled across the five announcement events the mean z is **+1.81
  with cross-event *t* = +0.60** and **1/5 positive** at K = 20, the sign flips with the
  horizon, dropping VXX turns the pool *negative* (*t* = −2.17), and the four
  curve-mismatched events are collectively negative — USO's 2020 suspension went the
  wrong way by **−19% in six sessions**. No pooled |*t*| reaches 2, so this is not Real;
  the surviving joint pattern in the one clean pair is too specific to call None.
  **Survivorship / selection is named here:** the event list is hand-curated from
  suspensions that were *reported*, which biases it toward spectacular premium blowouts,
  and two textbook cases (TVIX 2012, the pre-2018 VXX ETN) are missing outright because
  the instruments were redeemed and their tapes do not survive on Yahoo. The list is a
  survivor's list, and it still cannot pool.
- **Tradability — Mirage.** The audit killed the one number that looked bankable. On the
  hindsight exit VXX nets +17.80%; on a **blind 60-session hold — the only rule anyone
  could have followed — it nets +0.57%**. Ex ante you cannot tell a VXX from a USO
  (−19.5% net in six sessions on the identical trade), you cannot tell when the halt will
  end, and the premium round-trips to −1.1% by day 40 before returning. Median per-event
  net is **−4.29%** on both exit rules, 2/6 positive, cross-event *t* = +0.77 (hindsight)
  and +0.43 (blind); **ex-GBTC the mean is −4.51% with 1/5 positive**. The one number that
  decides the trade — the borrow on a hard-to-borrow, capped ETP — is unobservable and, at
  the 30%/yr such names actually cost, the mean net is **−27%**.
- **What is true, and worth keeping:** a creation halt *is* a real mechanical break in the
  arbitrage, and when you have an exact uncapped ruler you can see it plainly. What the
  tape refuses to support is the *tradable generalisation* — that halts, as a class, are
  buy signals — and what the blind exit shows is that even the one clean instance paid
  nothing to anyone who did not already know the ending.
